instruction.text: Find the relative clause in the sentence.

hint.text:
Relative clauses often start with a relative pronoun:

I bought a new car, which I am proud of.
Sam has a sister called Zoe, who is very friendly.
Kian has a dog, whose name is Tiggy.
The market, where we usually buy fresh fruit, is closing.
Last Christmas, when it was snowing, we went skiing.
Pearl was proud of her exam that she did last week.

atoms.b: Emma saw the dress ((that she wanted to buy)).

instruction.text: Now build the sentence without the relative pronoun.

hint.text:
You can have a sentence with a relative clause and not use a relative pronoun, but the sentence still has to make sense without it.
Sean ate the burger that he wanted for dinner. → Sean ate the burger he wanted for dinner.
